In response to a current crisis, some or all of your employees may have to stay away from the office and work remotely. Your job as a manager is to ensure they are supported and able to contribute productively while feeling connected and valued.

### Create clear processes
When you lead employees who work remotely either part-time or full-time, it's important to create clear processes. Clarify who they should reach out to for help on specific tasks, who they should collaborate with, and who they should report to when they complete their work. Make sure the details are clear so your team can work effectively on their own.

### Communicate often
Although remote work can be highly productive, it's easy for team members to lose sight of the big picture when they aren't in the office. Be sure to check in by chat, email, or virtual meeting to share key business details, just as you would if you were in the office. 

### Reinforce company culture
Companies that are successful with remote work value freedom and flexibility, while still having a high bar for performance. Remote work should not reduce quality or timeliness - work with each team member to discover the equipment, work schedule and flexibility they need to be most productive working remotely.
